gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-lao-looped: Towering lowercase like a stubby carpenter's pencil stroke gives Flavors its swagger, and Noto Sans Lao Looped settles in below it. Its words form solid blocks that read smoothly down the column.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Stubby, cheeky and tall: Flavors up top, Noto Sans Limbu beneath. Flavors does best at making a loud, same-gauge statement, while Noto Sans Limbu is better at carrying sentences in its gaping, tall-bodied letters.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Noto Sans Lisu brings generous s curves and tiny ascender gaps, a quiet counterweight to Flavors. Flavors makes the grand entrance, then the sans text carries the thought onward.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-lydian: Noto Sans Lydian keeps its capitals barely taller than its lowercase, which makes the text feel level and approachable. But over many lines it settles into an easy, wide-mouthed rhythm, with Flavors left to do the shouting.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-marchen: Stubby, towering, unmistakably Flavors, with diagonals as hefty as its stems. Noto Sans Marchen keeps its small letters proud and its curves open, so paragraphs keep moving without snagging.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-multani: Loud, stubby and sure of itself, Flavors ends every stroke at the same measured gauge. Noto Sans Multani, with a gapped e and lofty x-height, gives long reading a light, unhurried feel.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-nandinagari: Pencil-stub swagger, courtesy of Flavors and its constant-width pen line. Noto Sans Nandinagari brings generous openings at every weight, and that easy openness is what this pairing does best.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-old-permic: Neon-tube strokes, stubby and loud: that's Flavors in one glance. Flavors excels at constant-stroke display attitude, while Noto Sans Old Permic quietly handles rounded, open forms and lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-osmanya: Laser-etched, towering, a bit cheeky: that's Flavors. Noto Sans Osmanya sits underneath with wide, easy s turns and oversized lowercase, so the loud heading and the tidy text hand off smoothly.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-pahawh-hmong: Flavors does its best work loud, with a constant-width outline you could trace with a finger. Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong is the quieter worker, with a high x-height and rounds that gap like a cracked bangle.
